title: skills(objectui): optimization flight — contributor-only content moved out, duplicates merged into rules/, router first, three evals corrected (net −20,344 tokens, −31.8%)
body:
Fixes #7251

`skills/objectui/` goes from **64,023 to 43,679 tokens, −20,344 (−31.8%)**, 29 files to 27, across 12 commits — one per cluster, so any one can be dropped. Governed surface: this stays a **draft**; a human merge is the review record. `check:governed-queue-guard --test` returns exit 3 over the change set (28 of 31 paths governed), which is the correct verdict, not a red.

Audit record, finding by finding, is the second comment on #7251.

---

## Landing map — 落点 | before | after, by finding id

### (a) Contributor-only content out of the customer bundle

Consequential, each forced rather than chosen:

- `evals/console-development.json` (698 tok) deleted. The package's own rule, quoted from `README.md` before this PR removed that block: *"Removing or renaming a guide → rename the matching `evals/BASENAME.json` in the same change."* — the original spells `BASENAME` as an angle-bracketed placeholder, transliterated here because the body sanitizer eats that shape.
- `scripts/skills-path-baseline.json`: its single entry was keyed to the moved guide. The gate demanded the deletion in its own words — *"1 baseline entry the scan never met … Delete the entry from scripts/skills-path-baseline.json"* — which is the condition under which the dispatch put this file in scope at all. `allowedMissing` is now `{}`, with the reason recorded in its note.

F-01's premise re-measured: across the 437 schemas under `examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas/`, `flex` 248, `stack` 153, `box` 84, `container` 15 — the three most-used layout types, with **zero mentions package-wide**. Defaults in the table are the ones the **renderers** apply, not the ones the JSDoc claims (see the follow-up card). H-06's every `must_contain` token was checked to occur in the package text it grades.

## `premise_false`

**OUI-I-02 cluster ③ — the `data-table` / `useDataScope` reader trap. Merged, then reverted; the span is restored byte for byte from `96655c5`.**

The audit read the sections in `guides/schema-expressions.md` and `guides/data-integration.md` as copies 2 and 3 of a rule anchored in `rules/protocol.md`, noting they "share the Ada Lovelace / Grace Hopper fixture verbatim". They do — deliberately. Both spans are **executable fixtures**. `packages/components/src/__tests__/skill-guide-data-table-binding.test.tsx` lifts the bytes out of both files at run time and:

- requires exactly one parseable `data-table` block per guide, renders it through the real `SchemaRenderer` against a decoy dataSource, and asserts the four Ada/Grace body cells appear — transitively pinning the `accessorKey` column spelling, as its docblock records after objectui#5479;
- requires the literal sentence `the plugin packages register (…)` in each guide, extracts the seven `object-*` names, and asserts each is registered by exactly one plugin package reading `useDataScope(schema.bind)` — with an explicit counter-probe so an empty list cannot pass vacuously.

The merge deleted both fixtures: **5 assertions red**. The test says what the duplication is for:

> DOC-SAMENESS. The pin is on the guide bytes, not on a copy: the blocks are lifted out of the real files at run time, so re-introducing the defect in any of the three sites fails here.
>
> the guides are executable fixtures, so the instruction corpus cannot drift from the runtime without this file going red. **Keep it that way.**

Three sites are pinned because three sites are where the defect can come back. The other three I-02 clusters stand — prose in every copy, read by no test. Verified the same way that found this one: `git grep -ln skills/objectui -- ':!*.md' ':!skills/**'`, then running every test it names.

---

## Deviations from the audit's proposals, both forced by a repo rule the audit did not measure

**1. `compatibility` states no version literal (OUI-A-02).** The audit asked for the objectstack siblings' shape, `Requires @objectstack/spec 17.x (Zod v4 schemas)`. `scripts/__tests__/doc-version-claims.test.ts` refused it — that ratchet covers `skills/` (objectui#4981) and objectstack has no equivalent:

> These doc surfaces state a version and nothing in this repository can tell whether it is still true: `skills/objectui/SKILL.md:5 "@objectstack/spec 17.x"`, `"Zod v4"` … Prefer DELETING the literal and pointing at the truth instead … objectui#3645 froze `@objectstack/spec ^3.3.0` across 36 READMEs for thirteen major versions precisely because no review step ever asked this question.

The field now points at the manifests. A `KNOWN_CLAIMS` entry was rejected: registering a claim nothing can verify is what that ratchet exists to stop.

**2. `must_not_contain` spelling for OUI-H-03**, as noted in the correctness table.

---

## File surface — one supplement to the claim-declared list

`scripts/__tests__/check-skills-paths.test.ts` was co-edited, outside the dispatch's declared surface. It is a forced consequence of the ruled move, not a discretionary edit, taken under the bounded in-place rule and named here with its evidence:

- the `checked` floor `> 50` could not survive a scan that legitimately dropped to 27, so it is `> 20`, with the arithmetic (49 + 6 assertions left with the two moved files), the reason and the follow-up recorded beside it;
- the `objectui#3713 / #3730` block read the moved guide off disk through `repoRoot` and asserted the sole baseline exemption, so it threw ENOENT and then failed on an emptied baseline. It now pins the half that never needed the scan — the file still exists, still states more than 40 coordinates — plus an explicit assertion that it is **not** covered by the gate, written to be deleted the day `SCAN_ROOT` widens.

It landed inside `b38ee5e` rather than its own commit (a stale index entry); `72f650e` carries its full rationale rather than rewriting a pushed commit.

Tests, all serialized through the shared verify lock:

- `vitest run scripts/__tests__/{doc-version-claims,check-skills-paths,check-shell-escape-residue,check-control-bytes,check-governed-queue-guard,one-authority-per-exported-name-6273}.test.ts` → **`Test Files 6 passed (6)`, `Tests 155 passed (155)`**

**`pnpm lint` narrowing, declared.** Repo-wide eslint is CI's run. Narrowed here to the files eslint can judge, with the three readings that make the narrowing a measurement rather than a skip: ① the population comes from eslint's own config, not a guess — its `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx}']` block plus the ignore list; of the 31 changed paths exactly **1** is lintable by extension (`scripts/__tests__/check-skills-paths.test.ts`), the other 30 being `.md` and `.json`. ② `--format json` reports **1 file, 0 errors, 0 warnings**. ③ `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`, so linting is **not type-aware** and this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file.

## Changeset

None. The repo's own gate answered the question and is quoted above: *"No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed."* — 31 files changed, 0 published source of a released package, 0 manifests whose published contract moved. objectui has no `skip-changeset` mechanism and none was requested.

## Follow-ups

Filed unassigned, after a dedupe search on each:

- **#7358** — `check-skills-paths` lost 55 of its 93 assertions when the two guides left `SCAN_ROOT`. This is the honest cost of the ruled move, measured, with the widening's shape written down. The gate was built *for* `console-development.md` (#3713 / #3730), which is still 49 coordinates deep and now unguarded.
- **#7359** — no gate reads inside a code fence in this package: 123 TypeScript and 63 JSON fences, zero `os:check` markers. The flight's DEFER row **OUI-E-01**.
- **#7360** — six more eval assertions grade tokens their guide never teaches (**OUI-H-05**), plus **OUI-H-02**'s untaught `registerComponent` and `FieldWidgetProps` substring accident, plus one found here and not in the audit: `evals/mobile.json` eval 2 asserts `useOffline`, while the export is `useOfflineSync` — it passes on the substring.
- **#7361** — `finding`: two layout schemas' `@default` JSDoc disagrees with the renderer (`container.maxWidth` says `'lg'`, the renderer applies `'xl'`; `FlexLayoutProps.align` says `'center'`, `flex.tsx` applies `'start'` and `stack.tsx` `'stretch'`). An instance of #4631, found while writing the F-01 table from the renderers.
- **#7362** — `content/docs/guide/agent-skills.md` still draws both moved files inside the published tree, and `ci-cd-pipeline.md` describes a baseline entry that no longer exists. Outside this flight's file surface.

**Follow-up for objectstack-ui** (**OUI-A-01**): objectui routes outward — "those belong to the `objectstack-*` skills" — but nothing routes inward. objectstack's `skills/README.md` names objectui once, outside its Index and outside "Cross-skill routing". A customer on the objectstack bundle authoring Studio app UI has no route to this package for its core task. One "Cross-skill routing" row naming `@object-ui/*` renderer work would close it, in that repo.

**Follow-up for objectstack-ui / -data** (**OUI-C-05**): `@object-ui/permissions` is genuinely client-side and distinct from server RLS, but nothing in either package tells a customer **which to author**, and `auth-permissions.md` shows the trap — `RowLevelPermission.filter` is returned verbatim and uninterpolated, so `'ownerId = ${user.id}'` reaches the caller as literal text.
